messages:
samir: quick q — thinking about a lease-based approach to avoid duplicate prefix population when we miss the KV cache. proposal: acquire a short-lived lease per prefix (keyed by model+prefix-hash), first writer populates, others wait or stream from writer. avoids N backend inference spikes. thoughts? :thinking:

lucy: i like avoiding dup work. main worries: what if lease holder crashes mid-populate? also eviction interactions — we might evict the prefix while it's being populated and then commit stale data.

jamie: right — we need a commit protocol. basic idea: 1) acquire lease 2) write a tombstone/placeholder with meta {lease_id, expected_len, version} 3) populate KV (append chunks) 4) atomically flip placeholder -> ready with same version. readers treat placeholder as in-progress and either wait or fall back.

alexa: how do other replicas find out about the placeholder without thundering herd? if they see placeholder they should subscribe to updates or poll with exponential backoff. we should avoid busy-wait loops.

samir: agree. plan: short TTL on lease (default 5s), watchers get push notifications via pubsub on commit/abort. fallback path = if lease not acquired after N ms, callers can either 1) do local inference (slower) or 2) read-through from origin without caching. we already have streaming responses so callers can stream while population continues.

lucy: eviction semantics: if eviction runs and sees in-progress placeholder, eviction should either skip (honor lease) or increment a "evict-after-commit" flag. evicting mid-pop could cause partial blobs. commit needs to be atomic at namespace level.

jamie: implementation options for atomic commit: versioned keys (prefix#v123) + atomic pointer swap (prefix:current->prefix#v123). eviction operates on versions, not pointers. this simplifies rollbacks and read isolation during rollouts.

alexa: what about multi-host deployments (Dedicated/Private)? we can't rely on single-process mutexes. need a pluggable LeaseManager interface with implementations: in-memory for single-host tests, redis SETNX+expiry for hosted fast-path, and etcd/consul for enterprise installs where we want strong leases.

samir: yep — LeaseManager API minimal: TryAcquire(prefix, lease_ttl_ms) -> lease_id | nil, Renew(lease_id), Release(lease_id), Subscribe(prefix) -> chan events. keep it simple for consumers.

lucy: correctness tradeoffs: leases give us eventual progress but not linearizability. if we need strong semantics (no stale reads), we must couple versions with origin generation numbers or include model weights/version in key. that increases key churn though.

jamie: perf tradeoffs: more metadata and pubsub = memory + CPU. but prevents duplicate GPU runs which are far more expensive. need to measure hit/miss ratio inflection point where leases pay off. spike suggestion: simulate 1000 QPS with 10k prefixes, 5% cold miss rate, compare baseline vs lease approach for p50/p95 latencies and GPU cost.

alexa: failure modes: lease lost due to network split -> two writers. mitigate by making commit require verifying lease_id and version; if commit sees different lease, abort. also require idempotent population steps (chunked uploads with checksums).

samir: proposed heuristics: - default lease TTL 5s, renew up to 30s if population still ongoing - max waiters per prefix (to avoid pile-up) -> additional requests fallback to origin - eviction respects in-progress marker + has grace period = ttl + 1s - metrics: lease_acquire_rate, lease_conflicts, time_to_commit, evictions_during_lease

lucy: one more: how do rollouts interact? if model version changes mid-pop, we should namespace by model_version so old in-flight commits land in the old namespace; new requests go to new model_version. avoids cross-version contamination.

jamie: action items: 1) samir to draft short RFC with API definitions and failure scenarios (today) 2) spike: redis SETNX + pubsub prototype + benchmark (jamie + alexa) 3) add metrics to cache exporter for lease ops (lucy) 4) follow-up in eng-runtime sync next Wed.

alexa: +1 to spike. I'll prototype a minimal TryAcquire/Release using SETNX with value=lease_id and expiry. will also implement a simple placeholder pattern: key:prefix:meta -> {lease_id, status:"inflight", version} and key:prefix:chunks:<n>. commit flips status->ready and writes pointer.

mpo-bot: reminder: create a tracking ticket in rdx/eng-runtime -> "kv-lease-coordination + placeholder commit spike" and link PRs.

samir: thanks all. i'll write the RFC and include a few scenarios (process crash, network partition, eviction race). want to avoid coupling this to full refactor but propose extracting LeaseManager as separate package to keep options pluggable. :rocket:

lucy: sounds good. small nit: add abort metrics (leases_aborted) and alarms if aborts > 0.5% over 5m.

jamie: also capture fallback cost (tokens served without cache) in billing telemetry so we can quantify savings.

alexa: ok i'll start the prototype branch and ping here when I have a working SetNX + pubsub demo. :raised_hands:
